title: Smooth normalizers of subgroups containing a maximal-torus centralizer
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. All groups are affine $F$-group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and subgroups are closed subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness and connectedness are as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. A torus is a group isomorphic to $\mathbf G_m^r$ for an integer $r\geq0$, where $\mathbf G_m(A)=A^\times$ [def-sc-gm-ga]. A maximal torus is a torus subgroup maximal under inclusion. For a subgroup $S\subseteq G$, write $C_G(S)(A)=\{g\in G(A):g_{A\prime}s=sg_{A\prime}\text{ for every commutative }A\text{-algebra }A\prime\text{ and }s\in S(A\prime)\}$. Let $G$ be smooth and connected, let $T\subseteq G$ be a maximal torus, and let $H\subseteq G$ be a smooth subgroup, not necessarily connected, containing $C_G(T)$ as a subgroup functor. Define $$N_G(H)(A)=\{g\in G(A):g_{A\prime}H(A\prime)g_{A\prime}^{-1}=H(A\prime)\text{ for every commutative }A\text{-algebra }A\prime\}.$$ This functor is represented by a smooth closed subgroup scheme $N\subseteq G$ of finite type, and $N^\circ=H^\circ$ as subgroup schemes, where the superscript denotes the connected component containing the identity. The formula for $N_G(H)(A)$ holds for all commutative algebras, including nonreduced algebras. No reductivity or solvability hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Lemma 17.47, printed p.366; normalizer representability in Section 1j, Proposition 1.83 (deduced from 1.79), printed pp.30--31; Lie normalizer identity Proposition 10.34, printed pp.197--198.

proof.text: The schemes $G,H$ are separated: for any affine $F$-scheme $\operatorname{Spec}R$, the affine product formula [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies its diagonal with the surjection $R\otimes_FR\to R$, $a\otimes b\mapsto ab$. This is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], which is separatedness [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Thus $Y=H$, $X=G$, $S=G$, and $W=H\hookrightarrow G$ satisfy the separated finite-type hypotheses of the factorization theorem used next.

source.place: Proposition 1.83, pp.30–31, scheme hypotheses for its transporter construction; affine diagonal calculation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-constant-source-closed-factorization-locus] to the two morphisms $f_+(h,g)=ghg^{-1}$ and $f_-(h,g)=g^{-1}hg$, with source $H\times_FG$ and closed target $H\hookrightarrow G$. These are morphisms by the group operations [def-sc-group-scheme]. Obtain closed subschemes $L_+,L_-\hookrightarrow G$. If $G=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and their ideals are $I_+,I_-$, set $N=\operatorname{Spec}(R/(I_++I_-))$. By [def-weil-closed-immersion] and the affine ring-map description [def-weil-affine-spectrum], a map to $G$ factors through $N$ precisely when it factors through both $L_+$ and $L_-$. In particular $N$ is closed, affine and finite type: images of a finite set of generators of $R$ generate the quotient [def-weil-finite-type-morphism].

source.place: Proposition 1.83, printed p.31, N = transporter intersect inverse transporter; closed factorization locus Theorem 1.105, pp.37–38.

proof.text: For $g\in G(A)$ the two factorizations mean $gH_Ag^{-1}\subseteq H_A$ and $g^{-1}H_Ag\subseteq H_A$. Their conjunction is equality. Factorization implies both containments on every $A'$-point. Conversely take $A'=A\otimes_F\mathcal O(H)$ and the universal point of $H_A$: the corresponding point containment is exactly factorization of the coordinate map through the quotient defining $H$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-closed-immersion]. This proves precisely the displayed formula for $N_G(H)(A)$ for arbitrary, including nonreduced, $A$. Identity, multiplication and inverse preserve this condition: $(gh)H(gh)^{-1}=g(hHh^{-1})g^{-1}$ and the inverse reverses the equality. Thus $N$ is a subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Also $H\subseteq N$, since conjugation by an element of $H(A)$ permutes $H(A')$ for every $A'/A$.

source.place: Proposition 1.83, printed p.31: universal functor formula and subgroup property, made explicit on universal points.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-torus-centralizer-smooth-connected], the centralizer functor $C_G(T)$ is represented by a closed group $C$: $G$ is smooth connected and $T$ is a torus. The inclusion $C\subseteq H$ is a hypothesis. Since $T$ is commutative, $T\subseteq C\subseteq H$ on every test algebra. Apply [lem-sfb-lie-normalizer-centralizer-invariants] with $K=T$, and with the normalizer constructed above. Writing $\mathfrak g=\operatorname{Lie}(G)$, $\mathfrak h=\operatorname{Lie}(H)$, $\mathfrak n=\operatorname{Lie}(N)$, the injective tangent maps and the centralizer identity give $\mathfrak g^T=\operatorname{Lie}(C)\subseteq\mathfrak h$. The same node gives the rational $H$-action on $\mathfrak g/\mathfrak h$ and $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak h=(\mathfrak g/\mathfrak h)^H$. In particular $\mathfrak h$ is stable under $T$.

source.place: Lemma 17.47, printed p.366, first paragraph and Lie identities from Proposition 10.34, pp.197–198.

proof.text: Choose $T\simeq\mathbf G_m^r$. Apply [lem-sfb-gm-representation-weight-basis] to the first coordinate action on $\mathfrak g$, then to the second on each first-coordinate weight space, and so on. The coordinate actions commute, so each preserves the preceding weight spaces: apply the other coordinate to the defining equation $t\cdot v=t^av$. Induction on $r$, starting with the single space for $r=0$, gives $\mathfrak g=\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\mathbf Z^r}\mathfrak g_\alpha$. A $T$-stable subspace, in particular $\mathfrak h$, decomposes by the same weights: for $v=\sum v_\alpha$ in that subspace, evaluate the action at the universal tuple in $F[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}]$ and project to the quotient by the subspace. The equation $\sum \overline v_\alpha t^\alpha=0$ and linear independence of Laurent monomials force each $\overline v_\alpha=0$. This also identifies $\mathfrak g^T=\mathfrak g_0$: a nonzero exponent gives a Laurent monomial different from $1$, even in positive characteristic.

source.place: Theorem 12.12(d), Remark 12.13 and Example 12.15, printed pp.234–236; coordinate-by-coordinate specialization of the existing G_m weight-basis theorem.

proof.text: The quotient is therefore the direct sum of $\mathfrak g_\alpha/(\mathfrak h\cap\mathfrak g_\alpha)$. Its invariant subspace is its zero-weight summand, by exactly the universal Laurent-monomial coefficient test in the preceding step. Since $\mathfrak g_0=\mathfrak g^T\subseteq\mathfrak h$, this summand is zero. An $H$-fixed vector is $T$-fixed because $T\subseteq H$, so $(\mathfrak g/\mathfrak h)^H=0$. The normalizer identity of step 4 now gives $\mathfrak n/\mathfrak h=0$, hence $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak h$. This avoids replacing group invariants by Lie-algebra invariants.

source.place: Lemma 17.47, printed p.366, exact-sequence and invariants argument, written via the weight decomposition rather than an uncited exactness assertion.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-group-tangent-dimension-smoothness] first to the smooth group $H$ and then to the finite-type group $N$. The closed inclusion $H\subseteq N$ gives $\dim H\leq\dim N$: every chain of irreducible closed subsets of the closed subspace $|H|$ is a chain in $|N|$ [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Thus
$$\dim_F\mathfrak h=\dim H\leq\dim N\leq\dim_F\mathfrak n=\dim_F\mathfrak h.$$
All terms are finite, so equality holds. The criterion gives smoothness of $N$ and $\dim H=\dim N$.

source.place: Lemma 17.47, printed p.366, dimension inequalities using Proposition 1.37, printed p.18.

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-group-neutral-component-translates], $H^\circ,N^\circ$ are open and closed subgroup schemes and every component is a translate of the identity component. A finite clopen decomposition has dimension the maximum of its component dimensions (an irreducible chain lies in a single component). Thus $\dim H^\circ=\dim H=\dim N=\dim N^\circ$. The inclusion $H\subseteq N$ maps the connected set $|H^\circ|$ into $|N^\circ|$; its image is closed there. By [lem-sfb-locally-algebraic-group-identity-component], $N^\circ$ is irreducible and its reduced induced scheme is integral. It is affine, being closed in affine $N$. Apply [lem-wf-affine-dimension-drop] to this reduced affine variety: the equal dimension just proved rules out a proper closed image of $H^\circ$. Hence $|H^\circ|=|N^\circ|$. Finally [sbc-lem-smooth-geometrically-reduced], applied to the smooth groups $H,N$ over $F$, makes them reduced, and their open components are reduced by restriction of their local rings. They are closed reduced subschemes of $G$ with the same support; uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme](3) identifies them as subgroup schemes. Therefore $N^\circ=H^\circ$, as required.

source.place: Lemma 17.47, printed p.366, equality of identity components; Propositions 1.34–1.37, pp.16–18, and dimension argument as in Proposition 10.15, pp.190–191. Reduced closed structures: Stacks Tag 01J3, as in the cited node.

Step 4: the torus-centralizer node applies (F algebraically closed, so connected implies geometrically connected), and the new Lie node gives g^T=Lie(C)⊆h and n/h=(g/h)^H. Steps 5-6: coordinate-by-coordinate G_m weight decomposition using the existing weight-basis node; the decomposition of a stable subspace and g^T=g_0 are proved with Laurent monomials, valid in characteristic p; this gives (g/h)^H=0 and n=h. Step 7: the dimension chain of Milne 1.37 shows N is smooth. Step 8: components are translates, the dimension-drop node applies to the integral affine (N°)_red, so |H°|=|N°|; H° and N° are reduced closed subschemes, hence equal by Stacks 01J3 uniqueness.
